Chapter 12 of 19

Terminal Fog

harbour / citywide160 BPM
The story

The Repair People patch the city all day, one wall at a time. Some things cannot be patched. For those, Terminal City has the fog.

Late at night, after the after-hours rooms have emptied and the Freight has taken away what cannot stay, fog comes in from the water. It covers the shoreline, the tracks, the lights, the skyline, until enough of Vancouver is hidden for Terminal City to be rebuilt underneath. This is the full rebuild, the one that fixes what a brush cannot.

When the fog lifts, the city is back. Almost. One familiar thing is gone, or shifted, or slightly wrong, and nobody announces it. Then the crows fly out to inspect the new build, and the cycle returns to Trout Lake. Everything has returned so far. City ends. White line. No horizon. Start again.

Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented. Photograph reality. Alter the evidence. Never illustrate the whole myth.
